claims.text: The as-fabricated Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous fcc matrix.
The as-fabricated alloy has minimal pre-existing oxide content.
Elevated-temperature degradation in this alloy is governed primarily by selective oxidation of Cr and Ti.
Cr and Ti selectively oxidize because of the oxygen chemical potential in oxidizing atmospheres.
Selective oxidation produces a mixed scale that may contain Cr2O3 and Ti oxides.
The mixed oxide scale formed under oxidizing conditions is discontinuous and non-adherent.
Spallation of the non-adherent scale accelerates further oxidation.
Under reducing conditions, suppression of external scale formation promotes internal oxidation of Cr and Ti.
Internal oxidation under reducing conditions causes elemental segregation and compositional inhomogeneity.
Oxidation-induced segregation locally destabilizes the microstructure.
The alloy retains its global fcc phase during the proposed local oxidation and segregation processes.
The fcc matrix ensures good strength and fatigue performance in the as-produced state.
Oxidizing exposure will produce surface degradation and spalled, non-protective oxide scales relative to the unexposed baseline.
Reducing exposure will produce internal oxidation and segregation near grain boundaries or within the matrix.
Both oxidizing and reducing exposures will diminish fatigue resistance or strength relative to the unexposed alloy.
The proposed degradation becomes significant above approximately 900 degrees Celsius after roughly 100–200 hours.
Oxygen partial pressures above 0.2 atm define the applicable oxidizing condition, whereas pressures below 0.02 atm or a reducing mixture define the reducing condition.
Additive-manufacturing-induced microstructural heterogeneity may alter oxide-scale formation kinetics and adhesion.
